title: In the Absence of Knowledge
subtitle: Cache geometry separates real-entity from fake-entity prompts, a design label that it does not show to be knowledge (encoding-only equivalence unverified); the hedging-style choice is a coin flip at a balanced logit
abstract: KV-cache geometry separates real-entity from fake-entity prompts (a canonical template referent against a minor place name or category error; none of the fake entities is fabricated, the model answers several, and ten of 15 end in -ton) at AUROC 0.928, a bootstrap mean ([0.813, 0.988], not clustered by prompt pair; effective n 15 pairs; the fake prompt outscores its real partner in 15 of 15 pairs; 0.789 out of fold with the -ton suffix removed in-fold (bootstrap mean 0.754), within the range for 10 random fakes removed (median 0.807); 0.69-0.71 leave-one-template-out pooled, 0.94-1.0 within each template, matched by name-only baselines in the three templates whose fakes all end in -ton; on the nine fakes the model treats as real places in at least two of three runs (one unblinded reading) the classifier's call differs from how the model treats the name (answer correctness not checked), and removing corpus word frequency linearly in-fold leaves 0.947 out of fold (against 0.977 without; the 0.928 is a bootstrap mean); canonical fit is untested) (encoding-only: 0.9377 [0.8356, 0.9941], unverified; see Limitations) on token-matched prompts. If that unverified figure holds, encoding-only features achieve equivalent separation to the full classifier --- generation-phase features add no measurable discriminative power. On fake-entity prompts the model opens with a fixed reasoning template more often (34 of 45 generations against 20 of 45), and the mean logit margin of its first ten tokens is higher (d=0.91); within template openings the difference reverses (d=-0.56) and within the rest it is d=1.47, so template choice does not account for all of it. In three future-event prompts whose runs the regex splits between hedged and confabulated (the 3B judge labels all 21 responses of the seven such prompts HEDGED), the split begins at a single balanced-logit token and sampling determines the hedging framing; truthfulness was not scored. On 45 unanswerable questions (responses capped at 80 tokens) a three-judge panel flags 4 of the 15 fabricated-entity trials (a post-hoc restriction: its prompt's premise that the entity does not exist fails on the 30 future and unknowable ones, and it cut two of the five fabricated names short; a single 3B judge, 3/45), not the 73% of regex classifiers.
